Figgy Pudding

Served at: Twelfth Night

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 3 hours 30 min

Figgy Pudding, a rich, steamed dessert laden with dried fruit and spices, is a quintessential part of traditional British Christmas celebrations. Serving it on Twelfth Night marks the grand finale of the festive season, a sweet and warming conclusion to the revelry before the decorations come down. Its historical roots are deep, often associated with carols and merriment.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (150g) dried figs, stems removed and finely chopped
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) brandy or strong black tea
  • 1 cup (100g) fresh breadcrumbs
  • 1/2 cup (60g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100g) dark brown sugar, packed
  • 1/2 cup (100g) shredded suet (or cold butter, grated)
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • Zest of 1 orange
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) milk
  • For serving: Brandy butter or custard

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the chopped dried figs with the brandy or strong black tea. Let them soak for at least 30 minutes, or preferably longer, to plump up.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the breadcrumbs, flour, dark brown sugar, shredded suet, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, allspice, salt, and orange zest. Mix well to combine all dry ingredients.
  3. Add the soaked figs (and any remaining liquid), the lightly beaten eggs, and the milk to the dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly until everything is well combined into a thick batter.
  4. Generously grease a 1.5-quart (1.5L) pudding basin with butter. Spoon the pudding mixture into the prepared basin, pressing it down gently to remove any air pockets.
  5. Cut a circle of parchment paper slightly larger than the top of the basin and grease one side. Place it greased-side down over the pudding. Then, cover the basin tightly with aluminum foil, crimping it securely around the rim. You can also tie it with kitchen twine for extra security.
  6. Place the pudding basin on a trivet or a heatproof plate in a large pot. Pour boiling water into the pot until it comes halfway up the sides of the pudding basin. Bring the water to a gentle simmer, then cover the pot tightly.
  7. Steam the pudding for 3 to 3.5 hours, checking the water level periodically and topping up with more boiling water if needed. The pudding is done when a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
  8. Carefully remove the pudding basin from the pot. Let it cool for 10-15 minutes before inverting it onto a serving plate. Serve warm with brandy butter, custard, or a dollop of whipped cream.

Tips

  • This pudding can be made several days or even weeks in advance. Once cooled, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap and foil, and store in a cool, dark place. Reheat by steaming for 1-2 hours.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, replace the brandy with orange juice, apple juice, or strong black tea for soaking the figs and in the batter.
  • To serve flambéed, warm a few tablespoons of brandy in a small saucepan, ignite carefully, and pour over the pudding just before serving.
